   listed unit in its place because the listed one merely looks related (broader, narrower,

Symptoms analysis:
- Burning pain in stomach (epigastric pain)
- Gas and bloating
- Weight loss, loss of appetite
- Dark and tarry stools (melena) -> indicates upper GI bleeding
- Blood in vomit (hematemesis) -> indicates upper GI bleeding

These symptoms strongly point to Peptic Ulcer Disease (PUD). PUD often presents with epigastric burning pain, nausea/vomiting (sometimes with blood), melena (dark tarry stools due to digested blood), and weight loss due to fear of eating or malabsorption.

- gastroesophageal reflux disease: usually heartburn, regurgitation, but not typically hematemesis or melena.
- typhoid: fever, abdominal pain, diarrhea/constipation, but not typically hematemesis/melena.
- jaundice: yellowing of skin, dark urine, pale stools, itching.
